name: The Cauterized Sun

detectability.signature: An overwhelming X-ray and gamma beacon with a crisp periodic pulse; sensors classify it first as a star, then correct to something far worse.

proximity: Radiation dosages climb past emergency limits within the outer shell of dead plasma
Ship hulls glow faintly in the remnant's hard light, visible across thousands of kilometers
contact: Shield generators saturate and burn out within seconds at the inner boundary
Exposed materials begin sublimating under direct remnant radiation
prolonged_exposure: Any vessel at the core boundary is vaporized; there is no prolonged exposure, only distance
Approach beyond the inner shell results in total loss of ship and crew

phenomena: Light bending around the remnant's gravity well
Radiation spikes arriving in a metronomic 11-second pulse
Hull ionization and corona effects on vessels still tens of millions of kilometers out
hazards: Radiation exposure exceeding safe limits anywhere inside the dead plasma shell
Complete ship destruction within the inner boundary
Power system overload from the remnant's induced EM pulse train
opportunities: Unique research opportunity: the densest known stellar remnant outside charted space
Rare element concentration in the surrounding nebular slag fields
known_incidents: The colony ship Ossuar's Promise misjumped into the system in 2352; her lifeboat pods were recovered months later, their logs ending at first pulse contact
description: The Cauterized Sun is what remains when a star burns down to its stubborn heart: a sphere of white-hot degenerate matter nearly an astronomical unit wide, sheathed in a thin shell of its own dead atmosphere. It shines with the hard, steady glare of a forge left sealed shut, casting no warmth worth having. Every sensor in the system rings with its voice long before it is visible.

The remnant rotates once every eleven seconds, lashing the surrounding void with pulses of X-ray and gamma radiation so regular that ships set chronometers by it. Nothing about its behavior has drifted in recorded history; the danger lies not in surprise but in simple proximity, for its output falls off slowly and its reach is vast. Vessels crossing the outer shell of spent plasma accumulate lethal doses within hours, and the inner boundary permits no negotiation.

Deep survey flotillas found the remnant while tracing the asymmetric nebula that surrounds it, the scattered flesh of the star it once was. The colony ship Ossuar's Promise provided the only human encounter, a misjump that ended with lifeboat pods drifting in the slag fields, their logs cut short by the first pulse they met. Astronomers value the remnant as a natural laboratory for matter compressed past ordinary physics.

Mining consortia hold charters to the metal-rich slag fields orbiting far outside the hazard shell, worked exclusively by radiation-hardened drones. A listening station keeps permanent watch one light-hour distant, refining the pulse timing against some deep-time drift no one expects to find. Pilots crossing the system ride the narrow safe corridors between pulse geometry and the slag fields, treating the Cauterized Sun as a lighthouse that kills.
